core.definition: Che è senza compagnia, perché non ha nessuno con sé.

sentences.text: Oggi sono solo a casa, perché i miei genitori sono in vacanza.
Maria vive sola in un piccolo appartamento vicino alla stazione.
Quando sono solo, mi sento triste e non ho voglia di uscire.
I bambini sono rimasti soli in casa per un'ora, perché i genitori sono andati a fare la spesa.
Anna e Giulia non sono mai sole, perché hanno molte amiche.
La sera non voglio stare solo: puoi venire a cena da me?
Stasera mia nonna è sola, quindi la chiamo.
Mio fratello è timido e a scuola è spesso solo.
Dopo la festa tutti sono andati via e io sono rimasta sola.
Ho tanti amici, ma a volte mi sento solo.

options.explanation: Correct: this is the headword, /ˈso.lo/.
polo starts with /p/ where solo starts with /s/; the rest is the same.
volo starts with /v/ where solo starts with /s/; the rest is the same.
soldo adds /d/ after /l/, giving /ˈsɔl.do/.
suolo has the diphthong /wɔ/ in the first syllable where solo has a plain /o/.
Correct: soli agrees with I bambini and means without company.
semantic: alti means tall; children cannot stay tall in a house for an hour.
semantic: rotti means broken; it describes objects, not children who stay at home.
semantic: gialli means yellow; a colour cannot describe how children stayed home.
Correct: feminine plural, agreeing with Anna e Giulia.
This is the masculine singular; Anna e Giulia are two women, so feminine plural.
This is the feminine singular; Anna e Giulia are two people, so plural.
This is the masculine plural; Anna e Giulia are both women, so feminine.

wrong_sentences.text: Ho solo cinque euro, quindi non posso comprare il libro.
wrong_sentences.explanation: Here solo is the adverb 'only' (the same as soltanto) and limits cinque euro; it does not say that anyone is without company.

wrong_sentences.text: Oggi c'è il sole, quindi andiamo al mare.
wrong_sentences.explanation: Here sole is the noun 'sun', a different word that looks like the feminine plural of solo; nobody is alone.

wrong_sentences.text: Questa strada è molto sola di notte.
wrong_sentences.explanation: An empty street is deserta; sola is for people who are alone, not for places without traffic.

level_7.incorrect_sentence: Le mie sorelle sono rimaste sola a casa.
level_7.corrected_sentence: Le mie sorelle sono rimaste sole a casa.
level_7.error_description: Solo agrees with Le mie sorelle, so it must be feminine plural: sole, not sola.

options.explanation: Correct: accompagnato (with company) is the dictionary antonym of solo in this sense.
alto means tall and is not related in meaning to solo.
caldo means hot and has no antonym or synonym link with solo.
vecchio means old and is unrelated to solo.

preposition_selection.sentence: Maria vive sola ___ un piccolo appartamento vicino alla stazione.

options.explanation: Correct: vivere in un appartamento uses in for a building or dwelling.
a is used with cities and with casa (a casa), not with un appartamento.
su means on; it would put her on top of the flat, not inside it.
per means for or through; it does not say where someone lives.
Correct: this is the headword, /ˈso.lo/.
molo (a pier) starts with /m/ where solo starts with /s/; the rest is the same.
sodo (firm, hard-boiled) has /d/ where solo has /l/; the other sounds are the same.
sono (I am, they are) has /n/ where solo has /l/; the other sounds are the same.
Correct: sola agrees with Maria and means without company.
semantic: lunga means long; it describes objects or time, not a person who lives in a flat.
semantic: rotonda means round; a shape cannot say how Maria lives.
collocational: salata means salty and goes with food (la pasta è salata), not with vivere and a person.
Correct: feminine singular, agreeing with mia nonna.
This is the masculine singular; mia nonna is feminine.
This is the feminine plural; mia nonna is singular.
This is the masculine plural; mia nonna is feminine singular.

wrong_sentences.text: Sono figlio solo e non ho fratelli.
wrong_sentences.explanation: A child without siblings is figlio unico; solo does not mean only in this phrase.

wrong_sentences.text: Quella casa in montagna è molto sola e nessuno la visita.
wrong_sentences.explanation: A house far from others is isolata; sola is for people who are alone, not for buildings.

wrong_sentences.text: Ho visto quel film una sola volta, ma lo ricordo bene.
wrong_sentences.explanation: Here sola means 'only one' (una sola volta = just once), a different sense; it does not say that anyone is without company.

level_7.incorrect_sentence: Mio nonno vive sola in campagna.
level_7.corrected_sentence: Mio nonno vive solo in campagna.
level_7.error_description: Solo agrees with Mio nonno, which is masculine singular, so it must be solo, not sola.

preposition_selection.sentence: Ho tanti amici, ma ___ volte mi sento solo.

options.explanation: Correct: a volte is the fixed phrase meaning sometimes.
di volte does not form a phrase meaning sometimes.
per volte does not mean sometimes; per volta means each time.
da volte is not an Italian phrase.
